1.explanation: All of the problematic behavior lives in the React Pagination component. The method renderSelectItems(total) builds a <SelectItem> for each page up to totalPages, producing an impossibly long dropdown when totalPages is large. That dropdown is rendered in the render() function via a <Select> whose onChange is wired to handlePageInputChange. Because these pieces generate and display every page in a single Select, the UI breaks for large tables. To fix the UX, you’ll need to adjust renderSelectItems (or remove it entirely), stop using the <Select> for page numbers, and/or swap in a TextInput/NumberInput controlled by handlePageInputChange instead.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows that the page‐number selector is rendered as a native dropdown (<Select>) containing every page (1–69). When the table has many pages, the list of <SelectItem> options is far too long—it overflows the viewport, forcing the user to scroll the entire page to find the desired page. The request is to allow direct entry (for example via a TextInput/NumberInput) rather than an unwieldy Select list.

2.explanation: In the React Pagination component, the method renderSelectItems(total) generates a <SelectItem> entry for every page, creating a very long dropdown when totalPages is large. The <Select> in render() uses handlePageInputChange to process only select events, so end users cannot type a page number directly. To fix the UX, this code should be modified—either replacing the <Select> for page number with a NumberInput/TextInput or capping the number of items shown—so users can enter or jump to an arbitrary page instead of scrolling through an enormous list.
2.bug_scenario: The table’s page‐number selector is rendered as a long native HTML <select> listing every page (1, 2, 3, … 65, etc.). When the table has many pages, opening the dropdown produces a scrollable list that extends beyond the viewport, forcing the user to scroll inside the browser window just to find a given page. This is a poor user experience when there are dozens of pages.
